Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the draft SLA earlier this week. Procurement reviewed and we have two asks that are blockers for legal sign-off: 1) the fixed monthly credit cap (Section 5.2) — we need the ability to escalate credits for a one-off migration impact beyond the cap if total downtime exceeds the agreed threshold; and 2) a short-term latency exception during our planned data center migration window (two weeks) — we need a defined, documented exemption process rather than an open carveout.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: a) an escalation path that temporarily allows credits beyond the monthly cap subject to an internal review and b) a formal exemption workflow (owner, timeline, evidence required) so our risk team can close it out?

We attached the draft redlines from Legal and a spreadsheet with impact modelling. Happy to jump on a quick call today if that helps.

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Appreciated.

Short answer: yes, we can propose a controlled amendment. Outline below is what I can put into the SLA template for your legal team to review (I attached an edited draft):

1) Escalation for one-off events beyond monthly cap
- Add a temporary "exceptional remedy" clause: if cumulative outage or service-impact-related remediation in a single calendar month exceeds 150% of the monthly cap, parties may invoke an exception review within 10 business days.
- Exception review outcomes: additional credits (pro-rated) or invoice reconciliation subject to mutual agreement.
- Evidence: post-incident report, incident timelines, support tickets, and customer impact summary.

2) Migration / latency exemption workflow (short-term)
- Pre-notify: customer provides a migration calendar and expected impact window at least 30 days prior.
- Approval owner: Redwood CS (Marissa) will confirm operational plan and mitigation steps; legal will confirm carveout acceptance.
- Evidence required: test run results, mitigation checklist, and monitoring dashboard links.
- Duration cap: exemption applies only for the documented migration window (max 21 calendar days without separate amendment).

3) Credit scenarios (illustrative) — attached 'Credit_Calculator.xlsx'
- Minor impact: <1% monthly downtime = no credits
- Moderate: 1–3% = pro-rata monthly credits up to the cap
- Severe: >3% = trigger exception review with potential uplift beyond cap subject to review

If that framework works, I'll circulate a clean mark to your legal team and propose an inline change to Section 5.2 and a new Section 7.4 (Temporary Operational Exemptions). If you'd prefer different thresholds (e.g., 120% instead of 150%), we can adjust.

I attached: SLA_Draft_v3.pdf (redlines inline) and the credit calculator.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call this afternoon — available 3–4pm PT.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding AlphaTech's ask (below). Key decision points for us before I send the formal mark back:

- Threshold for escalation: I suggested 150% of monthly cap. Ben, do we have precedent for that number or should we push for 200%?
- Evidence package: Marissa, confirm CS can reliably produce the test-run artifacts and monitoring links within the 10-business-day review window. If not, propose adjustments to timelines.
- Duration cap: I put 21 days max for migration exemption. Laura, legal may want a hard stop at 14 days — any issues with being more conservative?

Notes on negotiation strategy: keep the exception process tightly scoped and time-bound. We can accept an exception review but insist on mutual agreement for uplift; escrow or invoice reconciliation gives us flexibility vs automatic payout. Also avoid language that allows "open-ended" credits beyond the cap without mutual sign-off.

Please reply with quick yes/no or redlines — I need to get a marked copy back to AlphaTech before EOD tomorrow.
